notice: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with Pyodide's Pillow 11.3.0 and NumPy 2.2.5 and the pytesseract 0.3.13 wheel the page carries, while the recording ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with pytesseract 0.3.13, Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4, OpenCV 5.0.0.93, PyAutoGUI 0.9.54 and the real Tesseract 5.3.4 (and 4.1.1 and 5.5.3 where a section says so). There is no Tesseract in a browser, so almost every example that reads text from a picture is shown as recorded: 66 examples are shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason, and 7 were run in the browser and match the recorded result value by value. Fifteen of the recorded ones need the zip of the book's online materials (ocr-example.png, frankenstein.png, frankenstein_jpn.png, preprocess_ocr.py), which a browser cannot download and this page does not embed (their licence has not been checked, and that is an open question); no picture made from them is on this page. The seven pictures under seven concepts are the recorded ones the research programs drew from sentences of their own; they were not made on this page. Windows, macOS, a flatbed scanner and a real screen were never used. Virtual display: the screen-reading program ran on a virtual X display (Xvfb) with ImageMagick's display and PyAutoGUI, a local stand-in for a screen, and nobody saw the picture. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 7, 15, 19, 22 and 23 NOT EXECUTED (slide 7: the Windows and macOS installers of Tesseract, Homebrew, and pytesseract 0.3.4, 0.3.7 and 0.3.8; slide 19: the Windows and macOS installers, the Flatpak of NAPS2 and a scanner; slide 22: a real screen with a real browser; slide 15: the chapter's step that sends the text to a large language model; slide 23: Python 3.15 final, those three pytesseract versions, a scanner, Windows and macOS), calls slides 4, 7, 12 and 23 Recorded (results of 13 October 2026 that it does not run again) and says on slide 22 that the screen-reading program ran on a virtual display with a local stand-in for a screen.

example_notes.pins: In your browser the Python is 3.13, where pkgutil.find_loader still exists, so the first result is (3, 13) and the second, hasattr(pkgutil, 'find_loader'), is True; the slide ran Python 3.14, which removed it, and printed (3, 14) and False. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.
example_notes.lang: In your browser this ends with TesseractNotFoundError at the first statement, because there is no Tesseract program to ask for its languages; the slide printed True and then (True, True, False) from the real Tesseract 5.3.4. Recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run on this page.
